newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi "oil-for-food" proceeds total $343 million.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi "oil-for-food" proceeds total $343 million.

text.p: Proceeds from the sale of Iraqi oil under an "oil-for-food" deal signed last December now total $343 million dollars, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Thursday.
This followed the receipt of $33 million on Monday and $7 million on Tuesday.

The deal enables Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The proceeds from the oil sales are paid into an escrow account at the New York branch of the Banque National de Paris.
Thirty percent of the proceeds are earmarked for a U.N. compensation commission, which deals with reparations for victims of the Iraqi invasion.
So far $113 million has been disbursed from the escrow account, including $72 million for reparations and the remainder to meet other costs stemming from the Gulf war, Eckhard said.
